title: Crypto-Asset Financial Crime: Typologies, Tracing and Controls
summary: An eight-module programme equipping supervisors, FIU analysts and investigators to recognise crypto-asset crime typologies, trace funds on-chain and assess service providers' controls.
topic: Reducing Financial Crime & Delivering Market Integrity
intro: This training programme equips supervisors, FIU analysts and investigators to recognise how crypto-assets are used to launder and move criminal proceeds, trace funds on-chain, and assess the controls that service providers should have in place.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors, FIU analysts and investigators a practical understanding of crypto-asset financial crime, from the main typologies and laundering techniques to how transactions are traced and attributed. Participants leave able to recognise red flags, test a service provider's due diligence and monitoring, interpret tracing evidence critically and decide on an effective supervisory or investigative response.
sections.What It Covers: Crypto-asset fundamentals for financial crime work, the FATF standards for virtual assets, criminal typologies, the laundering lifecycle on-chain, mixers and tumblers, privacy coins and unhosted wallets, blockchain tracing and attribution, customer due diligence and monitoring at service providers, the travel rule, suspicious transaction reporting, freezing and seizure, and international cooperation.
Intended Audience: AML/CFT supervisors and inspectors responsible for crypto-asset service providers
FIU analysts handling crypto-related suspicious transaction reports and intelligence
Law-enforcement and financial crime investigators working on cases involving crypto-assets
Learning Objectives: Explain how crypto-asset networks, wallets and service providers work and where financial crime risk arises
Identify the main typologies and red flags of crypto-enabled crime
Analyse how proceeds are placed, layered and integrated using crypto-assets and anonymity-enhancing tools
Interpret blockchain tracing and attribution evidence and recognise its limits
Assess service providers' customer due diligence, monitoring, travel rule and sanctions controls
Apply intelligence, freezing, seizure and cooperation tools to build an effective response
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a technical briefing with worked cases, red-flag exercises and supervisory or investigative questions, ending in an investigation workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the participants' roles.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of AML/CFT supervision, financial intelligence or financial crime investigation is helpful. No technical background in blockchain is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)

modules.title: Crypto-Assets and Financial Crime Risk: Foundations
modules.summary: The technical and regulatory grounding for financial crime work: how public blockchains, wallets and service providers operate, why they attract criminals, and what the FATF standards require.
objectives: Explain addresses, keys, transactions and public ledgers in plain terms
Describe the roles of exchanges, custodians, brokers and other service providers
Summarise the FATF standards and risk-based approach for virtual assets
syllabus: Blockchains, wallets, keys and transaction records
Service provider business models and points of fiat conversion
Pseudonymity, speed and cross-border reach as risk factors
FATF Recommendations 15 and 16 and the risk-based approach

modules.title: Typologies: How Criminals Use Crypto-Assets
modules.summary: The principal ways crypto-assets are used in crime, from fraud and ransomware to sanctions evasion and terrorist financing, with the red flags supervisors and investigators should look for.
objectives: Identify the main predicate offences and typologies involving crypto-assets
Recognise red flags in customer behaviour and transaction patterns
Assess emerging typologies and their implications for national risk assessments
syllabus: Investment and romance scams, fraud and money mule networks
Ransomware, darknet markets and cyber-enabled crime
Sanctions evasion, proliferation and terrorist financing
Red-flag indicators and feeding typologies into risk assessment

modules.title: The Laundering Lifecycle On-Chain
modules.summary: How criminal proceeds move through placement, layering and integration using crypto-assets, and where along the chain the best opportunities for detection and disruption lie.
objectives: Map placement, layering and integration to crypto-asset techniques
Explain chain-hopping, cross-chain bridges and decentralised finance as layering tools
Identify off-ramps and detection points where intervention is most effective
syllabus: Placement: cash-to-crypto, kiosks, peer-to-peer and over-the-counter brokers
Layering: rapid hops, chain-hopping, bridges, swaps and decentralised protocols
Integration: off-ramps, nested services, merchant payments and high-value assets
Detection points across the lifecycle

modules.title: Anonymity-Enhancing Tools: Mixers, Privacy Coins and Unhosted Wallets
modules.summary: How mixers and tumblers, privacy-enhancing coins and self-hosted wallets obscure the audit trail, what can still be seen, and the controls and supervisory responses they call for.
objectives: Explain how mixing, tumbling and coin-joining break transaction links
Describe how privacy coins and privacy features limit traceability
Assess service providers' policies on anonymity-enhanced transfers and unhosted wallets
syllabus: Custodial and non-custodial mixers, tumblers and coin-joining
Privacy-enhancing coins and privacy features: what remains visible
Unhosted wallets and peer-to-peer transfers: risk and controls
Red flags, enhanced due diligence and restrictions on exposure

modules.title: Tracing and Attribution: Blockchain Analytics in Practice
modules.summary: How investigators and service providers trace funds across public ledgers, cluster and attribute addresses, and how far analytics outputs can be relied on as intelligence or evidence.
objectives: Explain the main tracing techniques and clustering heuristics
Interpret risk scores, exposure reports and attribution data critically
Assess the evidential value and limits of analytics outputs
syllabus: Traceability on public ledgers: following inputs and outputs
Clustering, attribution and labelling of services and illicit actors
Risk scoring, false positives and gaps in coverage
From analytics to evidence: documentation, reproducibility and expert testimony

modules.title: Customer Due Diligence and Controls at Service Providers
modules.summary: What effective AML/CFT controls look like at crypto-asset service providers, and how supervisors test customer due diligence, wallet screening, transaction monitoring and travel rule compliance.
objectives: Assess customer due diligence and ongoing monitoring for crypto-asset customers
Evaluate wallet screening, transaction monitoring and sanctions controls
Test travel rule implementation and counterparty service provider due diligence
syllabus: Customer risk assessment, onboarding and source of funds and wealth
Wallet screening, transaction monitoring scenarios and alert handling
The travel rule: originator and beneficiary data and counterparty checks
Supervisory testing: sample selection, walk-throughs and common deficiencies

modules.title: From Intelligence to Action: Reporting, Seizure and Cooperation
modules.summary: How suspicious transaction reports become usable intelligence, how crypto-assets are frozen, seized and safely held, and how authorities cooperate across borders and with the private sector.
objectives: Evaluate the quality of crypto-related suspicious transaction reports
Explain the practicalities of freezing, seizing and managing crypto-assets
Use domestic and international cooperation channels effectively
syllabus: Suspicious transaction reporting: content, quality and FIU analysis
Freezing and seizure: private keys, service provider cooperation and custody
Asset management, valuation and return of seized crypto-assets
International cooperation, information sharing and public-private partnerships

modules.title: Investigation Workshop: Following the Funds
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a case exercise in which teams trace illicit funds, assess a service provider's controls and agree a coordinated supervisory, intelligence and enforcement response.
objectives: Apply typologies, tracing and red flags to a realistic case
Assess the control failures that allowed the funds to move
Agree a coordinated response across supervisor, FIU and law enforcement
syllabus: Case briefing: a fraud and laundering scheme across several service providers
Tracing exercise and red-flag analysis
Control failures and supervisory findings
Workshop: the joint response and action plan

related.title: The EU AML Package: AMLR, AMLD6 and AMLA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on the EU AML package for supervisors and firms: the AML Regulation single rulebook, AMLD6, AMLA's supervisory model, crypto-asset transfers and transition planning.

related.title: Asset Recovery: Tracing, Freezing and Confiscation
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping practitioners to trace, restrain, confiscate, manage and return criminal assets, including crypto-assets and assets held abroad.

related.title: Financial Crime Foundations for Regulatory Staff
related.summary: An eight-module foundation programme giving regulatory staff a grounding in AML/CFT, sanctions and fraud, firms' controls and financial crime red flags.

related.title: Financial Crime Supervision in the Age of AI
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess financial crime controls and firms' use of AI in monitoring, screening, fraud and surveillance.

related.title: Financial Investigation: Following the Money
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping investigators and analysts to run parallel financial investigations, trace funds through accounts and corporate vehicles, and present financial evidence.

related.title: FIU Operational and Strategic Analysis
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping FIU analysts to prioritise and analyse reports, produce operational and strategic intelligence, and cooperate effectively at home and abroad.
